key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform for excited-state simulations that combines GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and embedding methods without explicit virtual states.
engineering_relevance: For solar-cell and materials engineering, it enables practical prediction of optical excitations, quasiparticle energies, and excited-state dynamics in large, realistic systems such as perovskites.
method: Full-frequency GW and Bethe-Salpeter equation for quasiparticle and neutral excitations
TDDFT and quantum defect embedding in a common no-virtual-states framework
Hierarchical parallelization, GPU acceleration, and low-rank screening/exchange representations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs and successful applications to systems with more than a thousand atoms, including self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on sophisticated implementations and high-performance hardware, so workflow complexity may limit adoption in smaller computational environments.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
